find: \textit{Schechter Poultry} remains the \textit{only} Supreme Court decision ever to strike down a federal statute under the Article~I nondelegation doctrine.
replace: \textit{Schechter Poultry} remains the \textit{only} Supreme Court decision ever to strike down a federal statute for delegating legislative power to public officials. (A year later, \textit{Carter v. Carter Coal Co.}, 298 U.S.\ 238 (1936), struck down a delegation to private parties.)
reason: Overstatement. Carter v. Carter Coal also invalidated a federal statute as an unconstitutional delegation, to private producers and miners, and the brief itself relies on Carter Coal in Example 2 and the Private-Delegation paragraph. FCC v. Consumers' Research (2025) likewise says only two statutes have failed the intelligible-principle test, which is consistent with limiting the claim to public delegations.
source: https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/102662/carter-v-carter-coal-co/ ; FCC v. Consumers' Research, 606 U.S. 656 (2025), slip op. at 21-22 (only two)
